title: cam stats cycles: metrica de ciclo deterministica, versionada, emitida no cycle-close, + backfill dos 269 ciclos historicos
description: O event log esta gitignored: 7 semanas de historia (2026-06-09 a 2026-07-29), 86.805 eventos, 269 ciclos com cycleId, 16 MB, existindo so no disco de uma maquina, irrecuperavel e nao auditavel por terceiro. E sem comando de contagem o orquestrador estima em vez de contar: medido duas vezes em uma sessao (reportou check:all em 7min quando sao 4min37 / 277s, e 8 rodadas de gate por ciclo quando foram 5). Contagem e tarefa deterministica; nao deve ser feita por LLM. Solucao: subcomando cam stats cycles derivando uma linha por ciclo do log, arquivo derivado VERSIONADO (linha por ciclo, legivel e diffavel), emissao automatica no gancho de cycle-close que ja existe em src/commands/journal.ts:399-436, e backfill unico dos 269 ciclos existentes. Precedente a estender: src/commands/stats.ts (116 linhas, cam stats tokens, deterministico, mesmo log). NAO-OBJETIVO: SQLite. Parsear os 86.805 eventos leva 0,16s medido; o JSONL append-only e seguro para multiplos escritores (sidecar, worker, orquestrador so acrescentam linha) e o projeto tem cicatriz de escrita concorrente (colisao de next_id em issues.local.json). Banco, se entrar, entra como cache derivado reconstruivel, nunca fonte; gatilho: consulta acima de 2s, cruzar projetos, ou UI ao vivo. Motivacao: e a base de credibilidade da publicacao do lancamento (metodo como codigo + dado versionado = terceiro recalcula), numa area onde Factory AI e Warren publicam alegacao sem dado.

spec.scope: Add a `cycles` subcommand to `cam stats`, derive one row per attributed cycle from the event log, write the versioned artifact scripts/cam/cycle-metrics.jsonl (a schema-version header line plus one row per cycle), hang a best-effort emission step on the existing cycle-close sequence in dispatchJournal, and backfill every historical cycle. No database, no new subsystem, the raw event log stays gitignored. Re-spec of the version that escalated at the auditor on 2026-07-29 after 2 rounds: all 7 findings from that escalation are folded in, and 3 of them (F-01 head boundary, F-02 fixture-based value pins, F-03 downstream seeding) were defects in the previous spec text rather than in the planner's PRD.
acceptanceCriteria: The `cycles` subcommand exists and exits 0 against the repo's event log. [oracle: named-command bun index.ts stats cycles] SPECIES change-detection, swept RED on main 2026-07-29: exit=1, parseStatsArgs rejects any subcommand other than `tokens` and printFatalHint emits 'Usage: cam stats tokens'. Must-pass sanity on the same binary: `bun index.ts stats tokens` exits 0, proving the probe is not vacuous.

The derived artifact exists and is tracked by git. [oracle: named-command git ls-files --error-unmatch scripts/cam/cycle-metrics.jsonl] SPECIES change-detection, swept RED on main 2026-07-29: exit=1, path untracked. Must-pass sanity: the same command against scripts/cam/journal.md exits 0.

The artifact carries exactly one row per distinct cycleId that has an established left bound, i.e. the span before the FIRST cycle-tokens marker is not published as a cycle. [oracle: named-command test "$(jq -r 'select(.cycleId)|.cycleId' scripts/cam/cycle-metrics.jsonl 2>/dev/null | sort -u | awk 'END{print NR}')" = "$(jq -r 'select(.kind=="cycle-tokens")|.detail.cycleId' .claude/cam-worker-events.jsonl | tail -n +2 | sort -u | awk 'END{print NR}')"] SPECIES value, both sides derived live at check time, no frozen comparand. Swept RED on main 2026-07-29: exit=1 (artifact absent, left side empty). This is the F-01 detector: an implementation that folds the pre-instrumentation span into the first row publishes exactly one extra row (the head cycleId), so the two sides differ by 1. The `tail -n +2` on the right side IS the bounded rule expressed independently of the implementation.

The row for the hand-verified reference cycle SESSION-CAM466-2026-07-29 matches an independent re-derivation of the bounded slice, not a fixture the implementer wrote. [oracle: named-command test "$(jq -r --arg c SESSION-CAM466-2026-07-29 'select(.cycleId==$c)|[.workerRounds,.reviewRounds]|@csv' scripts/cam/cycle-metrics.jsonl 2>/dev/null)" = "$(awk -v c=SESSION-CAM466-2026-07-29 '/"kind":"cycle-tokens"/{ if (index($0,c)) { n=0; for (r in seen) n++; print ws","n; exit } ws=0; delete seen; next } /"kind":"worker-start"/{ws++} /"kind":"review-verdict-handback"/{ if (match($0,/"round":[0-9]+/)) seen[substr($0,RSTART+8,RLENGTH-8)]=1 }' .claude/cam-worker-events.jsonl)"] SPECIES value, comparand derived live by an awk reimplementation that shares no code with the feature. Swept RED on main 2026-07-29: exit=1. Verified green-side-correct before delivery: the awk derivation prints 5,3, which equals the figure hand-checked from the pane and the journal for that cycle (5 worker rounds, 3 review rounds). That value is immutable because the event log is append-only and this cycle closed on 2026-07-29. This criterion replaces the previous spec's `grep -q 'SESSION-CAM466-2026-07-29' <testfile>`, which proved only that a string existed in a file the implementer authored (F-02).

reviewRounds counts DISTINCT review rounds, not review-verdict-handback events. [oracle: named-command test "$(jq -r --arg c cam/pr-204-plan-block-replan-loop 'select(.cycleId==$c)|.reviewRounds' scripts/cam/cycle-metrics.jsonl 2>/dev/null)" = "$(awk -v c=cam/pr-204-plan-block-replan-loop '/"kind":"cycle-tokens"/{ if (index($0,c)) { n=0; for (r in seen) n++; print ws","n; exit } ws=0; delete seen; next } /"kind":"worker-start"/{ws++} /"kind":"review-verdict-handback"/{ if (match($0,/"round":[0-9]+/)) seen[substr($0,RSTART+8,RLENGTH-8)]=1 }' .claude/cam-worker-events.jsonl | cut -d, -f2)"] SPECIES value, comparand derived live. Swept RED on main 2026-07-29: exit=1. Deliberately discriminating: this cycle emitted 5 handback events carrying only 2 distinct rounds, so an implementation that counts events publishes 5 and fails, while the specified rule publishes 2. Measured: 9 of the 269 attributable slices carry duplicate rounds, because review-verdict-handback has two emit sites.

The artifact discloses the unattributed leading span explicitly, in the file, rather than folding it into a row or dropping it silently. [oracle: named-command test "$(jq -r 'select(.schemaVersion)|.unattributedLeadingEvents' scripts/cam/cycle-metrics.jsonl 2>/dev/null)" = "$(( $(grep -n '"kind":"cycle-tokens"' .claude/cam-worker-events.jsonl | head -1 | cut -d: -f1) - 1 ))"] SPECIES value, comparand derived live at check time. Swept RED on main 2026-07-29: exit=1. Measured today: 2207 events precede the first marker, a figure that is immutable because the log is append-only and only grows at the tail. This mirrors unattributedTokens, which the existing stats path surfaces as a distinct always-printed line rather than a silent drop or a fold.

The feature's own test suite exists and passes, with real assertions rather than a name grep. [oracle: named-command bun test test/commands/stats-cycles.test.ts] SPECIES change-detection, swept RED on main 2026-07-29: exit=1, the path does not exist. Must-pass sanity: `bun test test/commands/stats.test.ts` (the sibling suite for the existing tokens path) exits 0. The suite must cover, each as a named test: events before the first marker are not attributed to any cycle row; two markers sharing one cycleId merge into one row placed at the first marker's position; a cycle with no shipped ship-phase-result omits prNumber and mergeMode as absent keys rather than null or 'unknown'; reviewRounds counts distinct rounds; the incremental cycle-close upsert produces a file byte-identical to a full rebuild; and one cycle-close appends exactly one row with no manual intervention.
gotchas: F-01, the critical finding, and the reason this issue was demoted: the slice rule must be bounded on BOTH ends. A slice runs from the event AFTER the previous marker through the current marker. The span before the FIRST marker is not a cycle and must never be folded into the first row: the log starts 2026-06-09 while the first marker is 2026-06-29 (cycleId cam/CAM-96-hook-fail-closed-jq), so 2207 events belonging to roughly 26 pre-instrumentation cycles precede it. Recomputed from the real log under the unbounded rule, that first row would publish workerRounds 318 against 89 for the largest genuine cycle, in the exact artifact whose stated purpose is third-party recomputation. Mirror the local precedent instead: src/stats/tokens.ts:44-61 keeps unattributedTokens as a distinct field, and src/commands/stats.ts:93-103 prints it unconditionally (both branches push a line) with the comment 'flag unattributed spend rather than silently dropping or misattributing it -- this is a distinct line, always printed, never folded into any issue's row above'.

Consequence of the bounded rule that must be accepted explicitly rather than discovered later: in a fresh downstream project the very first cycle produces no row, because its left bound is unknowable from the log alone. The header's unattributedLeadingEvents figure discloses that span instead. This is deliberate. A rule that attributes the head span when it 'looks like one cycle' would be exactly the interval heuristic this issue forbids, and in this repo it would be wrong 26 times over.

reviewRounds is the count of DISTINCT detail.round values in the slice, never the number of review-verdict-handback events. That event has two emit sites (src/supervisor/loop.ts:1890 for the MAX_ROUNDS_DEBT promotion path and loop.ts:1926 for the normal handback), so a cycle can emit zero, one, or two events for the same round. Measured: 9 of 269 slices carry duplicate rounds, worst case cam/pr-204-plan-block-replan-loop with 5 events for rounds [1,2].

Do NOT publish quality-gate status on the row. buildResultDetail (src/supervisor/events.ts:802-811) records both gates as 'unknown' for every outcome except 'pass', which is the open defect CAM-444. This artifact must not inherit that defect in the fields it emits; omit gates entirely rather than publishing a field that is 'unknown' by construction.

prNumber and mergeMode exist only on the 'shipped' variant of ShipPhaseResult (src/supervisor/ship-runner.ts:117-126), which is flattened into detail at the emit site (src/commands/sidecar.ts:1342-1348), so detail.kind SHADOWS the envelope kind and must be selected on explicitly. Measured: only 200 of 269 attributable slices contain a shipped result. For the other 69, OMIT both keys; never emit null, and never emit 'unknown'.

cycleId is an OPAQUE free-form string, not the SESSION-<ISSUE>-<YYYY-MM-DD> shape the previous spec's domain term claimed. Measured over 270 markers: 71 are branch names shaped cam/*, 77 are DRAIN-*, 73 are a bare issue id shaped CAM-N, only 27 are SESSION-*, plus one-offs shaped SPEC-*, spec-batch-*, and operator-ceremony-*. Never parse it, never derive a date from it, never sort by it.

F-07: row order is the log order of each cycleId's FIRST marker. Without that rule the byte-identical-rebuild requirement is undefined, because 3 cycleIds carry two markers each (cam-152-flip-worker-spawn-container, cam/pr-187-commit-existence-gate, cam/pr-201-toolchain-parity) and the merged row's position would otherwise be ambiguous. One row per distinct cycleId, aggregates summed across its markers, row placed at the first marker's position.

The in-place upsert precedent is appendOutcomeToLine (src/commands/pattern-records.ts:338-369): it replaces the matched line in its original slot and pushes every other line back byte-for-byte, including blank and unparseable lines. suggestions.jsonl has NO upsert precedent (its writers only append with skip-on-duplicate, or delete whole lines), so pattern-records is the one to follow.

Emission slot in dispatchJournal: immediately after recordFn() at index.ts:1958, which is where the cycle-tokens marker the row derives from becomes durable, and strictly BEFORE armMarker() at index.ts:2027, because once the marker is armed the recycle watcher can SIGTERM this process mid-write. Keep it UNCONDITIONAL rather than gated on --cycle-close: recordCycleTokens itself is unconditional, so gating the row would let a plain `cam journal append` create a marker with no matching row and silently break marker-to-row parity. Wrap it in try/catch and warn only, exactly like the journal-archive and patterns-archive checks at index.ts:1996-2025, whose stated contract is that a throw or ok:false logs a warning and must never change the exit code or block marker arming and handoff. Inject it as a new optional field on JournalDispatchDeps (index.ts:1805-1866) with a module-level default fn, mirroring defaultArchiveFn.

F-03, resolved explicitly rather than left implicit: use the bootstrap-on-first-append posture and do NOT add a templates/ seed. Both postures exist in-repo. suggestions.jsonl is seeded empty by cam init and its absent-file branch is a hard printError (src/commands/suggestions.ts:167-176); pattern-records.jsonl has no seeding story and treats a missing file on main as an empty store whose first append bootstraps it, silently (src/commands/pattern-records.ts:12-15 and :119-133). The decisive reason to pick the pattern-records posture: cam init only materializes templates into the WORKING TREE (copyTemplates at src/commands/setup.ts:750-751, and setup.ts contains no git add or git commit anywhere), while an on-main appender requires the path to exist on MAIN, so a template seed would still land on the hard-error path in every fresh project. Because no template file is added, this issue needs no templates/ change and therefore no `bun run embed-vendor` regeneration.

Reuse the shared on-main plumbing, never a private copy: commitTreeToMain, checkMainUpToDate and pushMainBestEffort from src/git/on-main.ts. The module header at :328-332 states that new callers must import the shared exports and that adding another private byte-copy of the guards trips the jscpd gate. Parsing must follow the tolerant-reader contract already documented at src/stats/tokens.ts:14-16: malformed JSONL lines are skipped, never thrown on.

CLI wiring is four registration points, all typechecked: the ParsedStatsArgs union and STATS_USAGE at index.ts:2179-2195, which becomes 'Usage: cam stats tokens|cycles' mirroring PATTERNS_USAGE at index.ts:2062; a real mode switch in dispatchStats at index.ts:2209-2216, which today has none because mode is single-valued and it unconditionally calls the tokens fn; the Subcommands section of STATS_HELP at index.ts:1074-1102; and the top-level HELP entry at index.ts:136. Print an always-present unattributed-leading-span line and a machine-parseable CAM_STATS_CYCLES= handback line, mirroring CAM_STATS_TOKENS= at src/commands/stats.ts:112-114.

F-04: every CLI-behavior oracle here invokes `bun index.ts stats cycles`, never `cam stats cycles`. This deliberately supersedes the wording of the previous spec's AC1. Reason, per the curated oracle rule 5 in patterns.md (CAM-451/CAM-455): `cam` resolves to the installed binary, which is almost always older than the branch under test, so the criterion would go red for the wrong artifact and invite a bogus fix.

After the backfill lands, no feature branch may ever commit this file again: only the on-main appender writes it. A branch-side rewrite would clobber rows appended on main mid-cycle, which is the CAM-121 scar where a squash-merge clobbered issue writes made directly on main during the cycle.

F-05: do not freeze a volatile count into criterion prose. The previous spec froze 'the repo log currently carries 34 such trailing events'; the auditor recounted 35, and today it is 1, because a marker was appended at the tail. Every count referenced in the criteria above is either derived at check time or immutable by construction (a closed cycle's own figures, or the head span, which cannot change in an append-only log that grows only at the tail).
domainTerms: cycle-metrics row: one line of scripts/cam/cycle-metrics.jsonl, derived by code from the event log, versioned in the repo, describing exactly one attributed cycle, intended for third-party recomputation
attributed cycle slice: the run of events from the one after the previous cycle-tokens marker through the current marker; bounded on both ends, which is what makes the row honest

unattributed leading span: the events preceding the first cycle-tokens marker, which belong to no attributable cycle and are disclosed as an explicit count in the artifact header instead of being folded into the first row
cycleId: the opaque cycle key carried by detail.cycleId on cycle-tokens events, free-form in practice (branch names, DRAIN-*, bare issue ids, SESSION-*), never to be parsed or sorted
derived cache: the eventual role of any database in this design, rebuildable from the JSONL, never the source of truth
